studies.Reference: Choline and betaine intake and risk of breast cancer among post-menopausal women.
studies.Authors: Cho E, Holmes MD, Hankinson SE, Willett WC
studies.exposure_measurement_supporting_text: Nutrient intake was assessed using a validated food-frequency questionnaire six times since 1984.

extraction_supporting_text.sample_size: 74 584 post-menopausal women in the Nurses' Health Study.
extraction_supporting_text.effect_size: Participants in the highest quintile of intakes had multivariate relative risks of ... 0.98 (95% CI: 0.89-1.09; P-value, test for trend=0.96) for betaine, compared with those in the lowest quintiles of intakes.
extraction_supporting_text.effect_direction: Betaine intake was not associated with a reduced risk of post-menopausal breast cancer.
extraction_supporting_text.outcome_definition: 3990 incident cases of invasive breast cancer.
extraction_supporting_text.exposure_definition: Betaine intake was assessed using a validated food-frequency questionnaire.

studies.Reference: Serum betaine but not choline is inversely associated with breast cancer risk: a case-control study in China.
studies.Authors: Du YF, Lin FY, Long WQ, Luo WP, Yan B, Xu M, Mo XF, Zhang CX
studies.comparison_type: Q4 vs Q1 (highest vs lowest quartile of serum betaine)
studies.exposure_measurement_supporting_text: Serum choline and betaine were assayed by high-performance liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry.

extraction_supporting_text.sample_size: blood samples were available for 500 cases and 500 controls
extraction_supporting_text.effect_size: serum betaine (fourth vs first quartile adjusted OR 0.68, 95 % CI 0.47-0.97)
extraction_supporting_text.effect_direction: An inverse association with breast cancer risk was observed for serum betaine
extraction_supporting_text.p_value: Computed from the reported effect and 95% CI using a normal approximation: p=0.037.

studies.Reference: Choline and betaine intake is inversely associated with breast cancer risk: a two-stage case-control study in China.
studies.Authors: Zhang CX, Pan MX, Li B, Wang L, Mo XF, Chen YM, Lin FY, Ho SC
studies.exposure_measurement_supporting_text: A validated food frequency questionnaire was used to assess dietary intake by face-to-face interview.

extraction_supporting_text.sample_size: 807 cases and 807 age- (5-year interval) and residence (rural/urban)-matched controls.
extraction_supporting_text.effect_size: The adjusted OR for the highest quartile of intake compared with the lowest were ... 0.58 (95% CI = 0.42-0.80, P(trend) < 0.001) for betaine intake
extraction_supporting_text.effect_direction: A significant inverse association was found between dietary choline and betaine consumption and breast cancer risk.
extraction_supporting_text.outcome_definition: risk of breast cancer among Chinese women
extraction_supporting_text.exposure_definition: dietary intake of choline and betaine

headline.funnel_interpretation: Egger's test indicates no significant funnel plot asymmetry (p=0.1779). The distribution of studies appears symmetric, suggesting a lower risk of publication bias.
headline.results_interpretation: The pooled analysis of 3 studies yielded an effect size of 0.77 (95% CI: 0.56–1.07), indicating no statistically significant association between betaine and breast cancer. Although the point estimate suggests a potential inverse relationship, the confidence interval includes the null. These findings were accompanied by very high heterogeneity (I² = 81.92%), reflecting highly inconsistent results across studies.
